broken.what: The student's correct answer 'idk turn back on?' (heater switches back on when the room cools) was never acknowledged. The tutor jumped straight to LDRs.
The student asked 'whats ldr' and the tutor never said what LDR means (light-dependent resistor). It just repeated the resistance fact.
The correct answer 'low light intensity' was not confirmed. The tutor moved on to the test circuit without saying 'yes'.

Physics error: the voltmeter in the diagram measures the potential difference across the thermistor, not 'the push from the cell'. The word 'cell' was also used without being explained, which caused the S13 question.

Physics error: 'A cell is just a battery' is wrong at GCSE, where a battery is two or more cells. The tutor also answered its own question (resistance = V ÷ I) instead of letting the student try, then ended the lesson abruptly. The phrase 'both parts are non-linear' is unclear.
The 'Drawing a circuit to test a sensor' point was marked covered (4/4) although the student was never asked to draw or explain the circuit. The resistance step was never attempted by the student.

The two summaries contradict each other and the transcript. T13 says 'answered some on thermistors'; T14 says 'I told you about thermistors'. In fact the student correctly answered the thermistor question at S5 and the voltmeter question at S12.
S4 was correct ('it lets light out') but the test labelled it 'wrong'. The tutor accepted it correctly, but the test label is mislabelled.

looks_wrong.what: The circuit-symbols diagram in the opening panel is a tiny thumbnail. All symbol labels are unreadable without zooming.
The sidebar diagram thumbnail is so small that its labels are unreadable.
In the test-circuit diagram, the blue label 'water at a measured temperature' and the 'thermometer' and 'thermistor' labels are very small on the phone. They are hard to read without zooming.
The page heading 'What are you revising?' and the '← Home' button are cut off under the sticky header.
The 'Jump to' panel heading is scrolled off and cut under the top bar, so the list starts mid-panel.

fixes.change: Always explicitly confirm a correct student answer (e.g. S8 'turn back on', S11 'low light intensity') before introducing the next idea.
When the student asks 'whats X', give the full name and a one-line accurate meaning first: 'LDR = light-dependent resistor'; 'a cell is a single source of push; a battery is two or more cells'.
Say the voltmeter measures the potential difference across the thermistor, not the push from the cell.

fixes.target: Coverage logic for 'Drawing a circuit to test a sensor'
fixes.change: Do not mark the point covered or end the lesson until the student has attempted the R = V ÷ I step. Wait for their reply to 'what do we then work out?' instead of answering it.

fixes.target: Diagram rendering on phone (opening panel and test-circuit SVG)
fixes.change: Show the opening diagram at full width rather than as a thumbnail. Set a minimum label font size of about 14px in the test-circuit diagram.
